goal: Complete the single-page frontend route console so an engineer can change provider availability and immediately understand the active frontend implementer, why it was selected, and the ordered fallback path.
acceptance_criteria: Provide labeled native select controls for Codex, Z.ai, and Cursor. Each offers Available, Limited, and Unavailable states.
Recalculate on every select change and on initial load. Show the active route, a plain-language reason, ordered fallback routes, and a latest-event line.

Use this policy: prefer GLM-5.2 only when Z.ai is Available; otherwise prefer Terra when Codex is not Unavailable; otherwise prefer Composer when Cursor is not Unavailable; otherwise show that no implementation route is available. Include Sol High after Terra and Composer when Codex remains available.
Expose the selected route through an aria-live polite region. Every control is keyboard accessible with a visible focus state, and status meaning never depends on color alone.
Remain usable at 320 CSS pixels and 200 percent zoom. Include a structural mobile breakpoint and reduced-motion handling.
Use no external assets or dependencies. Keep all HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in index.html.
design_constraints: Product register. The physical scene is an engineer reviewing route health on a large monitor in a normally lit workspace, so use a warm light operations-manual surface.
Use the existing OKLCH tokens and a restrained color strategy. Use system sans and monospace only for model IDs or state values.
Create clear hierarchy with spacing, rules, type, and one contained decision surface. Do not turn every section into a card or use an identical card grid.
No gradients, gradient text, glassmorphism, decorative glow, side-stripe accents, hero metrics, custom form controls, or decorative motion.
No em dashes. Keep copy calm, exact, and concise. Do not claim a process is running.
Use 150 to 220 millisecond opacity or transform transitions only where they communicate state, with prefers-reduced-motion support.
avoid: Do not add files, packages, network calls, persistence, model invocation, architecture changes, or unrelated walkthrough content.
Do not use innerHTML, document.write, eval, or string-to-code execution.
Do not change the route policy described in the acceptance criteria.
